original_question: Which abelian pro-Lie groups are reflexive under Pontryagin duality, meaning that the canonical evaluation morphism from the group to the double dual is an isomorphism of topological groups?
target_in_paper: Section 4, Question 3: "Which Abelian pro-Lie groups are reflexive?" Read together with the immediately preceding definitions of \widehat{G}, \eta_G, semireflexive/reflexive, and the nearby context from Theorems 6 and 7. ([sidneymorris.net](https://sidneymorris.net/Morris156.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the paper's actual target almost exactly: it asks about the correct class of groups (Abelian pro-Lie groups), the correct duality framework (Pontryagin duality), and the correct notion of reflexivity, namely that the canonical evaluation map to the double dual be an isomorphism of topological groups. That is precisely the content of Question 3 once the paper's notation is unpacked. ([sidneymorris.net](https://sidneymorris.net/Morris156.pdf))
missing_details: The paper states this as an open problem—Question 3 in Section 4—not as a theorem or conjecture. ([sidneymorris.net](https://sidneymorris.net/Morris156.pdf))

The dual group is fixed as \widehat{G}=\operatorname{Hom}(G,\mathbb{T}) with the compact-open topology, where \mathbb{T}=\mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z}; your draft invokes Pontryagin duality but does not spell out this setup. ([sidneymorris.net](https://sidneymorris.net/Morris156.pdf))

The natural evaluation morphism is written explicitly as \eta_G(g)(\chi)=\chi(g); your draft refers to it descriptively but does not define it. ([sidneymorris.net](https://sidneymorris.net/Morris156.pdf))

The paper distinguishes semireflexive (\eta_G bijective) from reflexive (\eta_G an isomorphism of topological groups); that nearby definitional contrast is part of the local context for Question 3. ([sidneymorris.net](https://sidneymorris.net/Morris156.pdf))

To make the question fully stand-alone, it helps to say what an Abelian pro-Lie group is: equivalently, a closed subgroup of a product of finite-dimensional real Lie groups. ([sidneymorris.net](https://sidneymorris.net/Morris156.pdf))

The nearby context records the main solved case: every almost connected Abelian pro-Lie group is reflexive, and the remaining issue is reduced to groups with compact identity component, including prodiscrete groups. ([sidneymorris.net](https://sidneymorris.net/Morris156.pdf))

Theorem 6 gives the structural decomposition for arbitrary Abelian pro-Lie groups, including that G/G_0 is prodiscrete; this is part of the immediate setup before Question 3 and explains the paper's focus. ([sidneymorris.net](https://sidneymorris.net/Morris156.pdf))
refined_question: Characterize those Abelian pro-Lie groups G for which the Pontryagin evaluation morphism \eta_G:G\to\widehat{\widehat{G}}, defined by \eta_G(g)(\chi)=\chi(g), is an isomorphism of topological groups, where \widehat{G}=\operatorname{Hom}(G,\mathbb{T}) is equipped with the compact-open topology, \mathbb{T}=\mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z}, and an Abelian pro-Lie group means a closed subgroup of a product of finite-dimensional real Lie groups.
equivalent_formulation: Which Abelian pro-Lie groups are reflexive?
justification: Question 3 is the exact official formulation your draft is aiming at. Immediately before it, the paper defines the Pontryagin dual \widehat{G}=\operatorname{Hom}(G,\mathbb{T}) with the compact-open topology, the evaluation morphism \eta_G(g)(\chi)=\chi(g), and the meaning of semireflexive versus reflexive. Theorem 7 supplies the principal known case—every almost connected Abelian pro-Lie group is reflexive—and states that the unresolved part is reduced to Abelian pro-Lie groups with compact identity component; Theorem 6 gives the structural decomposition of arbitrary Abelian pro-Lie groups and shows G/G_0 is prodiscrete. So the sharp paper-faithful rewrite is a characterization problem for reflexive Abelian pro-Lie groups with these duality conventions fixed. ([sidneymorris.net](https://sidneymorris.net/Morris156.pdf))
